assumptions: Validated orthogonal capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation with spike-in controls are available.
Qualitative (non-numeric) pass/fail calls based on co-localization and detergent/protease sensitivity are acceptable gating criteria at this stage.
biological_rationale: High shear and transmembrane pressures encountered during scale TFF can mechanically damage vesicle membranes or mask surface epitopes; preserving membrane integrity is necessary to retain orthogonal, membrane-protected identity and potential EV-associated cargo. MISEV2023 and program preclinical findings highlight sensitivity of EV-associated measures to processing and the need for orthogonal analytics.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Orthogonal capture + fraction co-localization + protection assays
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Preserving a membrane-protected, capture-positive particle peak through concentration is necessary to attribute downstream activity to intact EVs and to enable comparability.

edges.competing_explanation: Assay interference or spike-in failure could mimic signature loss; spike-in and buffer-compatibility controls are required.
edges.missing_experiment: Matrixed TFF parameter study with orthogonal intact-EV analytics and explicit capture-reagent compatibility controls (including spike-in recovery).
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: guidance and program observations indicate processing sensitivity but do not quantify exact TFF parameter thresholds.

edges.competing_explanation: Even with preserved identity, delivery or species clearance could prevent in vivo recoverability; orthogonal in vivo bridging remains required.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recoverability tests using materials that pass/fail the TFF envelope identity criteria.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: preservation of analytic signatures is necessary but may not be sufficient for in vivo detectability across species (delivery/formulation factors may still dominate).

nodes.statement: High-flux / high-TMP TFF concentration conditions encountered during scale-up can cause shear- or pressure-induced alteration of EV membranes (loss of membrane integrity or epitope masking) without proportionate changes in bulk particle counts.

A staged low-shear concentration envelope (lower TMP/flux per cassette + inline gentle depth prefilter + cassette rotation) reduces the incidence of membrane alteration and preserves intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) compared with the standard high-flux TFF envelope.

Preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV signature after concentration enables use of that signature as an operational manufacturing gate for drug-substance definition and supports downstream potency and comparability assay development.

competing_explanations: Assay incompatibility, spike-in failure, or buffer interference may produce apparent signature loss independent of TFF conditions.
Upstream source-cell variability, fractionation method, or downstream formulation/device exposures may be dominant drivers of signature loss rather than TFF envelope.
dependencies: Analytical spike-in and capture-compatibility controls must be developed and validated before interpretation
Sufficient material volumes and TFF hardware scheduling for matched scale-proxy runs
design_question: At scale-relevant concentration steps, does replacing a single high-flux TFF cassette run with a staged low-shear TFF envelope (reduced TMP/flux per cassette + interim gentle depth-filtration step and cassette rotation) preserve an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature while maintaining manufacturable recovery compared with the current high-flux TFF envelope?
expected_measurable_effect: Samples processed under the staged low-shear TFF envelope will retain an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks and loss of capture signal after detergent + protease/RNase) while maintaining qualitatively acceptable particle/mass recovery compared with the high-flux TFF comparator.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow with density/SEC fractionation, particle counts per fraction, immuno-capture on intact fractions, detergent+protease protection testing, spike-in tracer readout, and protein:particle ratio measurement.
experiment.comparator: Staged low-shear envelope vs current high-flux TFF envelope run at equivalent processed volumes
experiment.control: Characterized small-EV positive control processed in parallel; buffer-only negative controls; spike-in recovery controls and capture-compatibility checks for buffers.
dependencies: Access to TFF hardware supporting programmable TMP/flux and cassette rotation
Validated capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible preservation of orthogonal intact-EV signatures in the staged low-shear arm across >=3 independent lots (with validated spike-in recovery), or spike-in tracer inconsistent across replicates.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, staged low-shear TFF envelope is not an effective mitigator of signature loss; deprioritize TFF-envelope modification and investigate alternative drivers (source-cell, fractionation, formulation/device).
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A staged low-shear TFF concentration envelope preserves intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) across independent lots at scale-proxy conditions, while high-flux TFF parameters produce reproducible loss of that signature despite similar bulk particle counts.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative preservation (yes/no) of co-localization between particle-count peaks and capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase in staged low-shear arm vs clear loss in high-flux comparator across >=3 lots; spike-in recovery demonstrating assay validity.
experiment.question: Does a staged low-shear TFF envelope preserve orthogonal intact-EV signatures and acceptable recovery compared with high-flux TFF?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from >=3 independent lots sufficient for matched scale-proxy runs
TFF system capable of controlled TMP/flux and cassette rotation
Exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS), iodixanol or SEC fractionation materials, protease/RNase, detergent (Triton X-100), total protein assay reagents
secondary_readouts: Recovered particle and mass yield (qualitative assessment for manufacturability)
experiment.success_criterion: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the staged low-shear envelope reproducibly shows particle-peak co-localization with capture-positive signal and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal, with spike-in recovery validating assays, while the high-flux comparator shows reproducible loss of orthogonal signature despite similar bulk particle counts.

explicit_inferences: Orthogonal intact-EV analytics (capture + fraction-level particle co-localization + protection assays) are more informative than bulk particle counts for assessing whether concentration preserves membrane-protected EVs.
A process envelope that preserves those orthogonal signals will reduce analytical ambiguity prior to committing to large-scale batch generation and bridging studies.
falsification_criteria: No reproducible qualitative preservation of orthogonal intact-EV signatures in the staged low-shear arm across >=3 independent lots (controls validate assay performance), or spike-in tracer fails to show consistent membrane-protected recovery (assay failure).
human_decisions_required: Approve allocation of conditioned-medium lots and TFF run time for comparative scale-proxy experiments
Approve capture-compatibility and spike-in control assays prior to main runs
manufacturability_assessment: Staged low-shear TFF modifications are implementable on manufacturing equipment (adjustable TMP/flux and cassette sequencing) and add modest operational complexity (controlled cassette rotation and inline prefilter) but are feasible; yield tradeoffs must be assessed qualitatively in scale-proxy runs.
manufacturing_rationale: Defining and enforcing an operational low-shear TFF envelope during concentration provides an actionable, process-level control that can be implemented at scale and assessed by orthogonal analytics prior to committing to GMP-like batches or bridging studies.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow applied to post-concentration outputs including: (1) density- or SEC-fractionation with particle-count per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture detection for canonical EV markers on intact fractions; (3) protease/RNase protection +/- detergent on captured material; (4) spike-in tracer recovery controls; (5) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; qualitative pass/fail co-localization calls (>=3 independent lots).
novelty_statement: This proposal shifts the substantive product-attribute under test from an assumed particle-count-based concentration metric to a process-envelope-controlled preservation of membrane-protected intact-EV analytical signatures at scale (i.e., operational TFF envelope as a manufacturing control). That change makes the discriminating experiment focus on orthogonal, membrane-protection analytics rather than bulk particle recovery alone.
principal_risks: Assay artifacts (buffer incompatibility, spike-in failure) may confound interpretation of TFF-envelope effects.
Even if identity is preserved at scale, intranasal delivery and cross-species biodistribution may remain limiting for translational success.
proposed_potency_relationship: Preservation of intact-EV identity after concentration is a prerequisite for developing mechanism-linked potency assays; it does not itself prove potency but enables more interpretable potency linkage experiments.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a scale-control operating envelope: staged low-shear TFF concentration (defined TMP/flux limits per cassette, cassette-rotation schedule, and an inline gentle depth prefilter) that demonstrably preserves orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) and provides acceptable qualitative yield for downstream bounded small-EV drug-substance definition.
title: Define scale-control TFF envelope to preserve intact-EV analytical signature during concentration
